newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to back renewal of Iraq oil deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to back renewal of Iraq oil deal.

text.p: The United States will support United Nations renewal of the Iraqi "oil-for-food" deal, which expires on June 7, a source familiar with the decision said on Monday.
The source, who asked not to be identified, said the United States "will be looking favourably toward the rollover, but the vote (in the U.N. Security Council) won't be for a couple of days."

Earlier, a State Department spokesman said the Clinton administration would decide later this week whether to back a six-month renewal of the deal, which temporarily waives a U.N. ban on oil sales imposed after Iraq's 199O invasion of Kuwait.
Under the humanitarian waiver, Iraq is allowed to sell up to $2 billion worth of oil in order to get money to buy food and medicine.
"We will study the issue closely and make our determination closer to the time of renewal," spokesman John Dinger told reporters.
U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan has recommended that the oil-for-food deal, which first went into effect last December, be renewed on the same terms.
Most members of the Security Council, which must approve renewal of the deal, have said they would like to see the agreement approved under current terms or even increased.
The U.S. mission to the United Nations concurred with Annan's recommendation, the source said.
U.S. officials stressed that Secretary of State Madeleine Albright would make the final decision. "But nothing has occurred to want to make us revisit policy on this," one official told Reuters.
"There is a humanitarian need and a political need" for further Iraqi oil sales, the official said.
Dinger reiterated U.S. criticism of the Baghdad regime and its failure to adhere to U.N. Security Council resolutions.

"We're very disappointed with continued attempts by the regime in Baghdad to evade the procedures that are laid down in the memorandum of understanding that governs Resolution 986 (the oil-for-food deal)," he said.
He added that Washington was "disappointed" by recent Iraqi statements that blamed the United States for the hardships facing the Iraqi people.
"It is very clear that there is only one party responsible for the suffering of the people of Iraq, and that is the regime of Saddam Hussein," Dinger said.
Iraq's situation could be improved if the regime stopped threatening regional stability and paved the way for removal of the U.N. sanctions, the State Department spokesman said.
